doc.title: VATSIM DC SFRA Procedures
doc.summary: How the Washington DC SFRA and FRZ are handled on VATSIM: transponder rules, SFRA positions and gates, SFRA flight plan filing, and VFR exit, entry and pattern procedures.

items.title: SFRA/FRZ overview; not for real world use
items.text: The Washington SFRA and FRZ are TFR-published airspaces around Washington D.C. requiring constant ATC communication and special flight plans. This document gives the real-world context and the procedures emulated on VATSIM. Further reading lists FAA SFRA course notes, kneeboard checklists (DC SFRA, JYO), the FAA training course and an Open Sky Aviation presentation. Not for real world use.

items.title: SFRA and FRZ dimensions
items.text: The SFRA extends 30nm from the DCA VOR, surface to FL180. The FRZ is a more localized area of approximately 15nm radius including DCA, ADW, CGS, DAA and VKX. Real-world entry requires an SFRA flight plan, beacon code and online training course. Diagram 1 also shows W50, GAI, BWI, FME, 3MD4, W00, ANP, MD22, MD14, 2W5, NYG, IAD, HEF and JYO inside the SFRA.

items.title: Leesburg Maneuvering Area: VFR to/from JYO
items.text: The Leesburg Maneuvering Area is a cutout of the SFRA over Leesburg (JYO). Aircraft operating directly from or directly to JYO under VFR within the Leesburg Maneuvering Area boundary need not file an SFRA flight plan, nor contact ATC when Leesburg Tower is closed.

items.title: FRZ treated as SFRA; pattern work allowed
items.text: Real FRZ procedures (PIN, background check, phone flight plan, no pattern work or loitering) are impractical on VATSIM, so the FRZ is treated as simply another area of the SFRA. Pattern work and normal VFR operations shall be permitted within the FRZ on VATSIM.
items.restr: Pattern work and VFR permitted in FRZ

items.title: SFRA equipment: two-way radio and Mode C
items.text: Within the SFRA, regardless of flight rules, aircraft must have an operable two-way radio capable of communicating with ATC on appropriate frequencies and an operating automatic altitude reporting transponder. Pilots must also comply with the requirements of the underlying airspace.

items.title: No 1200 in SFRA; discrete code required
items.text: At no time should an aircraft squawk 1200 within 30nm of the DCA VOR. Aircraft should obtain and continuously transmit a discrete beacon code anytime in the air, except: VFR traffic pattern at a Class D airport 1234; VFR directly from/to JYO within the Leesburg Maneuvering Area 1226; departing a fringe airport without an SFRA flight plan and without ATC communication 1205.

items.title: Class D VFR pattern: squawk 1234
items.text: When flying in a VFR traffic pattern at a Class D airport within the SFRA, squawk 1234.

items.title: Fringe airport departure w/o SFRA FP: squawk 1205
items.text: When departing from a fringe airport without filing an SFRA flight plan and without ATC communication, squawk 1205. Fringe airports are not listed in the document.

items.title: NORDO / no transponder in SFRA: controller actions
items.text: If an aircraft fails to meet SFRA transponder or communications requirements, controllers shall: use ".contactme"; verbally inform the pilot that ATC communication is required in the SFRA; send DC SFRA pilot resources by private message; notify VATSIM Network Supervisors of possible B3(a) and/or B8(b) violations (e.g. ".wallop N123AB NORDO within DC SFRA"); and coordinate with available vSOA members for interception if desired and workload permitting.

items.title: SFRAE (CHP) 132.775, STARS 1Z: WOOLY/PALEO
items.text: SFRA East position SFRAE, area CHP, frequency 132.775, STARS handoff 1Z. Diagram 1 shows it covering the WOOLY and PALEO gates (north/east sector, including W50, GAI, BWI, FME, CGS, 3MD4, W00, ANP, MD22). When closed, consolidates to BWIFS 119.700.

items.title: SFRAW (SHD) 127.325, STARS 3G: LUCKE/JASEN/FLUKY/BRV
items.text: SFRA West position SFRAW, area SHD, frequency 127.325, STARS handoff 3G. Diagram 1 shows it covering the LUCKE, JASEN, FLUKY and BRV gates (west sector, including JYO, IAD, HEF, DAA). Consolidation order: SFRAW 127.325, then BARIN 128.525, then MULRR 126.100.

items.title: SFRAS (MTV) 125.125, STARS 1R: GRUBY/WHINO
items.text: SFRA South position SFRAS, area MTV, frequency 125.125, STARS handoff 1R. Diagram 1 shows it covering the GRUBY and WHINO gates (south sector, including VKX, 2W5, MD14). Consolidation order: SFRAS 125.125, then DEALE 128.350, then KRANT 125.650, then OJAAY 119.850.

items.title: SFRA sectors own no airspace; IFR/FF handling
items.text: SFRA sectors own no airspace; they track VFR aircraft in their portion of the SFRA and issue discrete beacon codes. Aircraft wanting an IFR clearance are transferred to the correct radar sector for their airport. For VFR flight following, the SFRA sector creates a flight plan with all information (aircraft, altitude, destination, departure, gate) and hands off to the correct radar sector with coordination.

items.title: Closed SFRA positions: assumed by area controller
items.text: When SFRA positions are not open, controllers assume the SFRA positions within the areas they are responsible for, using the consolidation table (Diagram 2) if multiple sectors in an area are staffed: CHP: SFRAE to BWIFS; SHD: SFRAW to BARIN to MULRR; MTV: SFRAS to DEALE to KRANT to OJAAY. There is no SFRA position in JRV.

items.title: IFR from nontowered SFRA airport: no airborne pickup
items.text: When departing from a nontowered airport, aircraft are not permitted to depart VFR and pick up an IFR transponder code and clearance in the air.

items.title: IFR to nontowered SFRA airport: keep code until landing
items.text: When arriving at a nontowered airport, aircraft keep the discrete transponder code until on the ground, even after terminating radar services or canceling IFR. Phraseology: "Remain on the code until you land."
items.restr: Remain on the code until you land

items.title: SFRA flight plan: file IFR with gates in route
items.text: Pilots file an IFR flight plan to operate in the SFRA even if VFR, so vNAS generates the discrete code and controllers see the type and gates. File departure and destination as normal and specify the entry/exit gates in the route, e.g. "DEP/PALEO DEST/LUCKE". For pattern work file the airport code plus "360001", e.g. "GAI360001". Aircraft may enter and exit anywhere within the area of the filed gate. RMK/SFRA in remarks is optional.

items.title: VFR SFRA exit: code and frequency before departure
items.text: Pilots file an appropriate flight plan and obtain the discrete code and departure frequency before departure. Non-towered airport: contact the respective SFRA frequency (e.g. "Skyhawk 123AB, Potomac Clearance, squawk 5367, departure frequency 132.77"). Class D airport: contact ATC before taxi (e.g. "Manassas ground, squawk 0227, departure frequency 127.32. Advise ready to taxi"). Class B airport: no SFRA-specific VFR departure procedure.

items.title: VFR SFRA exit: 'transponder observed, remain outside Bravo'
items.text: Pilots contact Potomac once clear of the airport traffic area, normally within 2-3 nm. Radar services are not provided: say "transponder observed" instead of "radar contact", and instruct "proceed on course, remain outside the Bravo" as the authorization to operate in the SFRA.
items.restr: Transponder observed; proceed on course, remain outside the Bravo

items.title: SFRA FF / Class B transition: APREQ, new code
items.text: If the aircraft requests flight following or a Class B transition, the SFRA position must APREQ the appropriate non-SFRA position and a new transponder code is issued for radar identification.

items.title: VFR SFRA exit: advise leaving SFRA, squawk VFR
items.text: The pilot is advised when departing the SFRA and the SFRA flight plan is considered closed ("you are outside the SFRA, squawk VFR, frequency change approved"). If tracked by a non-SFRA position for flight following, the controller may keep the aircraft for further services.

items.title: VFR SFRA entry: code first, remain outside SFRA
items.text: Pilots file an appropriate flight plan and obtain the discrete code from the appropriate SFRA position before entering. On initial contact, issue the code and instruct to remain outside the SFRA (e.g. "Skyhawk 123AB, squawk 4755, remain outside the SFRA"); if unfamiliar, issue suggested VFR headings to keep clear.

items.title: VFR SFRA entry: proceed on course, remain outside Bravo
items.text: Upon observing the transponder, instruct "proceed on course, and remain outside the Bravo" as the authorization to operate within the SFRA; "cleared into the SFRA" may be added for emphasis. No further action is needed if tracked by a non-SFRA position with flight following.
items.restr: Proceed on course, remain outside the Bravo

items.title: VFR SFRA entry: switch to local, keep code to landing
items.text: Switch the aircraft to local or advisory frequency near the destination and instruct it to keep the transponder code until landing. The SFRA flight plan closes on landing; no further action is required.

items.title: VFR pattern ops: FP only if tower closed/nontowered
items.text: If the tower is open, no SFRA flight plan is required for VFR traffic pattern operations. If the tower is closed or the airport is non-towered, the pilot files an SFRA flight plan (airport code plus 360001) and obtains a discrete code from Potomac TRACON before departure.
items.restr: Tower closed: SFRA FP + discrete code
